site.name: Strategy Arena
index.title: How do you really play?
index.lead: {n} short strategic games. At the end you get a profile measured from what you actually did, not from a questionnaire: how many steps ahead you think, how you react to unfairness, how much you trust, how you handle risk.
index.card1: About 3 minutes. No money is involved: you play for points. Your opponents are real choices made by other players, never bots or made-up answers.
index.card2: This is a research project. Your anonymous choices help build an open model of how people actually decide. You must be 18 or older.
index.welcome_back: Welcome back. A new set of games is ready. Playing again also shows how your choices change over time.
consent.title: Before you play
consent.collect: What we collect: your choices in each game, how long each choice took, the language you play in, and, only if you choose to tell us, your age band, country and education level.
consent.dont: What we don't collect: your name, email, phone number or IP address. You get a random ID stored in a browser cookie.
consent.use: How it's used: anonymous research on how people make strategic decisions. Data is shared with researchers only in anonymised form and is never sold.
consent.rights: Your rights: you can stop at any time and delete everything from the "Delete my data" link.
consent.agree: I have read the above and agree to take part.
consent.optional_p: Helps us check whether people in different places decide differently. Skip anything you like.
consent.error: You need to confirm both boxes to play.
play.answer_step: Your answer ({min} to {max}, in steps of {step})
matrix.intro: You and another real player each choose an option without seeing the other's choice.
matrix.cell: You choose {mine}, they choose {theirs}: you get {me}, they get {them}.
profile.title: Your strategic profile
profile.lead: Measured from what you did. Percentiles compare you with everyone who has played.
profile.lead_few: Measured from what you did. Comparisons with other players appear once a few more people have played.
profile.results_p: Points in each game against real choices by other players. "Pending" means nobody has played the other role yet.
profile.share_p: This link shows your profile card only: no ID, no answers, nothing that identifies you.
profile.changes_p: Differences between the first time and the latest time you played the same games.
profile.next_set_p: A different set of games is ready. Come back any time: replaying shows how your choices change.
trait.reasoning_depth.name: Steps ahead
trait.reasoning_depth.why: From your number guess: level 0 guesses around 50; each step of reasoning about others multiplies by two-thirds.
trait.depth_1120.name: Steps ahead (11–20 game)
trait.depth_1120.why: Asking for 20 is level 0; each point lower is one more step of thinking about what the other player asks for.
trait.fair_offer_pct.name: Generosity
trait.fair_offer_pct.why: How much of 100 points you offered a stranger who could reject it.
trait.min_accept_pct.name: Fairness line
trait.min_accept_pct.why: The smallest share you'd accept rather than leave both of you with nothing.
trait.dictator_pct.name: Giving
trait.dictator_pct.why: How much you gave away when the other player had no say at all.
trait.trust_pct.name: Trust
trait.trust_pct.why: Share of your points you sent to a stranger.
trait.reciprocity_pct.name: Reciprocity
trait.reciprocity_pct.why: Share you'd send back to someone who trusted you.
trait.cooperation_pct.name: Cooperation
trait.cooperation_pct.why: Share you put into the group project.
trait.bid_shading_pct.name: Bid shading
trait.bid_shading_pct.why: How far below your value you bid in the pay-your-bid auction.
trait.truthful_bid_pct.name: Bidding your true value
trait.truthful_bid_pct.why: In the second-price auction, bidding exactly your value is the best strategy. 100% means you did.
trait.loss_aversion.name: Loss aversion
trait.loss_aversion.why: How much bigger a win must be than a loss before you take a coin flip. 1 means even odds feel fine.
trait.pd_cooperate.name: Cooperated when it was risky
trait.pd_cooperate.why: In a game where each player gains by not cooperating, did you cooperate anyway?
trait.stag.name: Went for the big shared prize
trait.stag.why: Did you choose the option that pays most only if the other player does the same?
trait.hawk.name: Played tough
trait.hawk.why: In a game of chicken, did you choose the aggressive option?
trait.price.name: Price you set
trait.price.why: Against a competing seller, lower prices win buyers but earn less each.
trait.effort.name: Team effort
trait.effort.why: Your effort when the whole team is paid by its weakest member.
trait.claim.name: Lost-luggage claim
trait.claim.why: Claiming high trusts the other player to claim high too; the rational-agent answer is the minimum, 20.
game.beauty.title: Guess two-thirds of the average
game.beauty.player: Pick a whole number from 0 to 100. Your number is compared with the numbers picked by up to 9 other players. Whoever is closest to two-thirds of the average of all these numbers wins 100 points.
game.ultimatum_offer.title: Split 100 points
game.ultimatum_offer.proposer: You have 100 points to split with another player. You offer them part of it. If the smallest offer they said they would accept is at or below your offer, you keep the rest and they get your offer. Otherwise you both get nothing. Your result is decided by another real player's answer to that question.
game.ultimatum_min.title: Accept or reject a split
game.ultimatum_min.responder: Another player has 100 points to split with you. What is the smallest offer you would accept? If their offer is lower, you both get nothing. Your answer is matched with a real offer made by another player.
game.trust_send.title: Trust a stranger
game.trust_send.sender: You have 10 points. Whatever you send to another player is tripled. They then send back a share of what they received. How many points do you send? Your result uses another real player's choice of what share to send back.
game.trust_return.title: Return the favour
game.trust_return.receiver: Another player could send you some of their 10 points, and whatever they send is tripled. What percentage of what you receive would you send back to them?
game.public_goods.title: The group project
game.public_goods.member: You are in a group of 4 with three other players. Each of you has 20 points. Every point anyone puts into the group project pays every member 0.5 points. You keep whatever you don't put in. How many points do you put in?
game.auction.title: Sealed-bid auction
game.auction.bidder: An item is worth {value} points to you. You bid against one other real player, whose value was a random number from 1 to 100. The higher bid wins and pays its own bid; you earn your value minus your bid if you win, and nothing if you lose. What do you bid?
game.m_coord.title: Meet in the middle
game.m_other_dom.title: Read your opponent
game.gambles.title: Coin flips
game.gambles.player: For each coin flip, choose whether to play. Heads you win the amount shown; tails you lose 10 points.
game.dictator.title: Share or keep
game.dictator.giver: You have 100 points. You can give any part of it to another player, who has no say in it. How many points do you give away?
game.pd.title: Two options
game.stag.title: Big or safe
game.hawk_dove.title: Who backs down
game.hide_seek.title: Hide and seek
game.second_price.title: Second-price auction
game.second_price.bidder: An item is worth {value} points to you. You bid against one other real player, whose value was a random number from 1 to 100. The higher bid wins but pays the other player's bid; you earn your value minus their bid if you win, and nothing if you lose. What do you bid?
game.bertrand.title: Set your price
game.bertrand.seller: You and another seller sell the same product to 10 buyers, and it costs you nothing to make. You each set a price from 1 to 10 at the same time. All buyers buy from whoever is cheaper; if your prices are equal you split the buyers. Your points are your price times the buyers you get. What price do you set?
game.weakest_link.title: Weakest link
game.weakest_link.member: You are in a group of 4 with three other players. Each of you picks a number from 1 to 7. Your points are 60, plus 20 times the smallest number anyone in the group picked, minus 10 times your own number. What number do you pick?
game.money_request.title: The 11–20 game
game.money_request.player: Ask for any whole number of points from 11 to 20; you get what you ask for. You also get a bonus of 20 points if your number is exactly one less than the other player's number. How many points do you ask for?
game.travelers.title: Lost luggage
game.travelers.claimant: You and another player each lost an identical suitcase, and each of you claims its value: 20, 30, 40 and so on up to 100 points. If you claim the same amount, you both get it. If the claims differ, both get the lower claim, plus 10 for whoever claimed lower and minus 10 for whoever claimed higher. What do you claim?
share.title: A strategic profile
share.lead: Measured from how they actually played: real games, real opponents, no questionnaire.
withdraw.title: Delete my data
withdraw.body: This permanently deletes every choice you made and the optional details you gave. It can't be undone.
withdraw.none: This browser has no data stored with us. If you played on another device or cleared your cookies, contact us with your anonymous ID and we'll delete it.
withdrawn.title: Deleted
withdrawn.body: Everything linked to your anonymous ID has been removed. Thanks for playing.
privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.draft: Version {v}. Draft for review by the project's ethics committee and a lawyer before public launch.
privacy.who: A student research project building an open model of how people make strategic decisions. Contact: https://polymetis-pjkz.onrender.com/#pilot.
privacy.what1: Your choices in each game, how long each took, and the language you played in: this is the research data.
privacy.what2: Optional age band, country and education level: to study differences between groups.
privacy.what3: A random ID in a browser cookie: so your choices stay linked across visits and you can delete them.
privacy.not: We do not collect names, emails, phone numbers, precise location or IP addresses.
privacy.basis: Your explicit consent, given before you play, under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. You can withdraw it at any time; withdrawal deletes your data.
privacy.share: The research team. Anonymised, aggregated data may be published or shared with other researchers. If you share your profile card, anyone with that link sees the card's traits, never your ID or answers. We never sell data and never use it for decisions about you.
privacy.keep: Until the research ends or you delete it, whichever comes first.
privacy.rights: Access, correction and deletion: use "Delete my data", or email us with your anonymous ID. Complaints can also go to the Data Protection Board of India.
game.bonus.title: Bonus game
play.bonus_note: Three quick bonus games for the research, at the end of every visit. Same rules: real opponents, points only.
